reason: Long disaster and failure videos from small channels break out (Fault Lines, 11K subs: 1.94M on a 10-min 3D crash reconstruction), the long trend is rising (4.96), and the quality references hold 400K-1.1M medians; but a flood of new low-effort channels sits at 30-300 views, so it only works at high craft.
conditions: Craft before volume (owner, 20 Nov): no sample ships unless it beats the references' first minute; the new low-effort channels in this scan get 9-285 median long views.

No repeated look (owner): a look-rotation and novelty gate in QA that fails a video whose kit mix, palette, camera language or place set repeats a recent video's; every video mixes kits (flat 2D, 3D, doc kit with real photos and report documents).
Long videos 8-10 min (owner's choice, 20 Nov, over the data's 10-15 min best band: on-niche 10-15 min median 775 vs 6-10 min 285), one every 48 h + 1 promo Short each; 8+ min keeps mid-rolls.
3D only for the key 60-120 s per video (the moment of failure): cloud 3D renders about 3.75 s a frame, so a full 3D long video would take 15+ hours; the rest in 2D and the doc kit.
Settled, sourced stories: official investigation reports (NTSB, AAIB, BEA, ATSB, TSB, CSB) and reputable outlets; recent events told from preliminary reports only, with no blame beyond the report.
Respectful and advertiser-friendly: no gore, no bodies, no victim close-ups, no sensational 'horror' thumbnails; deaths stated plainly, ending on what changed.
for: Small channels break out on long video: Fault Lines Official (11K subs) 1,941,409 and 551,482 views at 10 min; Engineering Revealed (2.5K) 389,157 and 228,073 at 15 min; Major Disasters (420 subs) 185,887; BUILT TO HOLD (842 subs) 159,148.
Proven demand at the top: 90-day long medians Practical Engineering 1,144,945, Fascinating Horror 635,479, Plainly Difficult 401,670 (10-11 min videos); the long trend is rising (direction 4.96).
Good money for the views: transport and education niches have the top median RPMs in AIR's 300-channel data ($5.69 transport, $10.22 education; estimates); 10-15 min videos carry mid-rolls.
against: Supply is rising fast at the bottom: about 12 new channels (6-842 subs) post 5-47 long videos each at 9-285 median views; 'low supply' holds only for well-made videos.
The 3D reconstructions that drive the biggest small-channel hits render slowly in the cloud (about 3.75 s a frame); 3D must be limited to key moments or rendered on the PC.

YouTube's bar doubles to 8,000 watch hours on 1 Feb 2027; reaching 4,000 before then needs about 50K long views in 10 weeks, so a hit, not the plan; tragedy topics can get limited ads if told graphically.

earnings.assumptions: Estimates, not facts. One long video every 48 h (about 15 a month, 10-15 min) + 1 promo Short each. Partner programme at 8,000 watch hours (bar from 1 Feb 2027): about 90K long views at ~5.5 min watched, reached in month 3-5 in 'likely' (sooner with one breakout), never in 'low'. Long RPM $5 likely (AIR transport median $5.69, education $10.22; estimates); Shorts ignored. m6 likely: ~60K long views a month after joining. m12 likely: ~300K a month (15 videos x ~20K, small-channel hits 150K-1.9M as upside). High: one Fault Lines-sized hit a month. Sponsors not counted.

demand.note: On-niche channels only (20; news, Indian politics and fact channels the searches caught are excluded). The long median (353) is dragged down by ~12 new tiny channels posting many low-view videos; quality references: Practical Engineering 1,144,945, Fascinating Horror 635,479, Plainly Difficult 401,670. Raw scan: long 23,026, Shorts 35,163, best band 10-15 min 69,187. smallChannelsWithHit = on-niche channels under 50K subs with a 10K+ video in 90 days.

doable.look: Every kit combined per video: 3D (remotion/src/three) for the moment of failure, flat 2D (remotion/src/flat) for maps, cutaways and the timeline, the doc kit (remotion/src/doc, generator/media) for real photos, report pages, diagrams and headlines. Build items: a look-rotation and novelty gate, a 3D vehicle/structure set (plane, ship, train, bridge, building kit pieces), a cockpit-voice and radio transcript prop, and a flight/route path tool on the 2D map.
doable.voice: Kokoro narrator (calm documentary voice, American or British English); the references are calm narrated documentaries, so a TTS narrator fits. Never voice a real person's words (cockpit recordings, witnesses) with TTS: show them as transcript text.
doable.policy: Inauthentic content (judged channel-wide) -> original research and scripts, varied looks per video. Advertiser-friendly: educational tragedy coverage earns ads; graphic injury or sensational framing gets limited ads. US government reports and diagrams are public domain; other countries' reports cited, not reproduced in full; photos from Commons with credits. Synthetic-content label when a realistic reconstruction of a real event could be mistaken for footage.

ownerDecisions.cadence: one long video every 48 h + 1 promo Short per long
